tiers.name: web-toolchain
tiers.holds: The build and test toolchain every package's own `vitest.config.ts` and `tsup.config.ts` extends: the workspace-root presets, plus the two that happen to sit inside `features/` — a shared preset is toolchain wherever it physically lives, and longest-prefix matching is what lets those two files say so without moving. This is the one thing packages legitimately reach up to, so it is its own foundation tier rather than part of the `web-workspace` catch-all; otherwise every package in the repo reads as importing upward. Paths are spelled without extensions because a relative import resolves that way. Not shared: config to extend, not components to build on.

tiers.name: apple-project
tiers.holds: The Xcode/SwiftPM scaffolding around the frameworks: the workspace and xcodeproj, their shared schemes, project.yml, the Makefile, .swiftlint.yml and .swiftpm mirrors. Longest-prefix match sends every framework directory to its own tier, so only the build scaffolding lands here.

tiers.name: platform-stubs
tiers.holds: Placeholders for targets that do not exist yet — a .gitkeep under packages/android/ and packages/windows/ and nothing else. Named platform-stubs rather than android or windows because a tier name is matched against import specifiers.

tiers.name: web-workspace
tiers.holds: The pnpm workspace itself: package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml, the lockfile, .npmrc/.npmignore, copy-css.mjs and the web README. Configuration for the packages below it, not code they import.

tiers.name: web-tools
tiers.holds: Python maintenance scripts run against the workspace by hand — content extraction and validation, and the chat-types copy verifier. They read the tree; nothing in the tree imports them.

tiers.name: vendor
tiers.holds: Submodule checkouts of sibling repos consumed as shared packages, declared in shared_packages above. Their contents belong to their own repo and their own map — never edit them here. Named vendor, not external, because a tier name is matched against import specifiers.

tiers.name: repo-docs
tiers.holds: Design specs, plans, research and the project overview, including docs/web/ which holds the web stack's own layering table. Prose. Named repo-docs, not docs, to keep the tier name off any import specifier.

tiers.name: repo-meta
tiers.holds: How this repo is worked on rather than what it ships: the agent instructions, CI workflows, git's own files, the top-level README, the submodule install script and this tier map.

tiers.name: component-recipes
tiers.holds: The component catalogue — one dated, versioned markdown recipe per shared component (button, dialog, data-table, crud-table…), each naming the package that owns it. Prose, and the human-readable index of what web-ui and its siblings already export: read it before proposing a new component.

tiers.name: repo-scripts
tiers.holds: Repo-level guards run by hand and in CI, not imported by anything. check_boundaries.py enforces this repo's OTHER layering rule, orthogonal to the tiers here: packages named @agentic-toolkit/adh* are the adh VOCABULARY tier and portable MECHANISM packages may never import them. Its banned set is discovered from package.json names, never listed.

tiers.name: repo-tools
tiers.holds: One-off maintenance scripts run by hand against the repo itself — currently the recipe classifier that sorts `recipes/` by component tier. Nothing imports these; they are invoked, not built on.
